app: TextEdit — hard-text stress (ligatures, combining accents, CJK, RTL Arabic/Hebrew, bidi, ZWJ emoji)

stack_detection.method: bundle id + AX text area exposes parameterized text attributes
stack_detection.signature: com.apple.TextEdit; AXTextArea advertises AXBoundsForRange / AXRangeForPosition / AXStringForRange

channel_setup: A UTF-8 file written by the harness (10 hard cases, one per line) is the ground truth; opened in TextEdit and read back through AXValue plus parameterized text attributes. Direct counterpart to the Linux glyph-decode cell, which had to reconstruct text from glyph IDs.

t1_read_text.detail: 10/10 EXACT, byte-for-byte against the source file, with no normalisation applied by the channel: presentation-form ligatures (U+FB01/U+FB02 in 'ﬁche ﬂux œuvre'), precomposed accents ('café naïve Noël'), COMBINING accents (e+U+0301, i+U+0308 — preserved as combining, not silently NFC-folded), CJK ('你好世界 こんにちは 한국어'), RTL Arabic and Hebrew, bidi-mixed ('Total: 42 مرحبا END') returned in LOGICAL order, simple emoji, and ZWJ sequences (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 family, 👩🏽‍💻 with skin-tone modifier). Read latency 0.03 ms. THE STRUCTURAL POINT: on macOS the sanctioned channel hands over the model string, so the entire glyph-decoding pipeline the Linux render-tap needed (reverse cmap + NFKC + BiDi reorder, with a lossy tail on custom ligatures) simply does not arise. The trade-off is the mirror image: AX reports the text the app HOLDS, not the glyphs it PAINTED — a font-fallback failure would be invisible to this channel, where the render tap would show it.

t2_enumerate.detail: Text geometry is fully addressable: AXBoundsForRange returns the on-screen rect of any substring. Verified against the screenshot — the pure-RTL lines are right-aligned (Arabic at x=770 w=86, Hebrew at x=797 w=59, both ending at x=856 against a window right edge of 866) while Latin starts at x=220. In the bidi-mixed line the three runs resolve left-to-right as 'Total:' [220,40], 'مرحبا' [286,33], 'END' [326,20] — the Arabic word sits in the middle with its glyphs internally reversed, and the API resolves it correctly.

t5_blind_action.detail: The INVERSE mapping works too, which is what an agent needs to aim inside text: AXRangeForPosition at the centre of each run returns the exact character under that pixel — 'a' for the centre of 'Total:', 'N' for the centre of 'END', and 'ح' for the centre of the Arabic word (the correct middle letter of مرحبا despite right-to-left glyph order). Text↔geometry is a closed round-trip through the channel.

t6_pictorial.detail: No pictorial region in this document.

measurements.notes: The whole hard-text document is 139 code points; the window it fills is 656x422 logical; its actual 2x capture (1312x844 px, the artifact) costs 1477 image tokens — 42x the structured view of the same content. RANGE-ARITHMETIC TRAP, measured: AX ranges are in UTF-16 units while Python/JS string indices are code points, and the gap is large exactly where it hurts — '🦊 🎯' is 3 code points but 5 UTF-16 units, '👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 👩🏽‍💻' is 12 code points but 19 units. Worse for layout reasoning: the family emoji occupies ELEVEN UTF-16 units and renders as ONE 15x18 px cell, so string length is not a proxy for visual extent in either direction. Any harness doing offset math must convert explicitly.

runtime_verification.method: decoded strings compared byte-for-byte to the source file; geometry cross-checked against a window screenshot (right-aligned RTL lines, single-cell family emoji), and the point->character inverse verified on three runs of the bidi line
runtime_verification.agreement: exact on all 10 cases; geometry and inverse mapping agree with the screenshot

permissions_required: Screen Recording for the verification screenshot
